new_findings.finding: The README guard added by this commit is self-contradictory and fails on the very commit that introduces it. It allows the README's recorded commit to lag HEAD by up to MAX_CSA_LAG (1), but then asserts the README's recorded divergence equals `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` computed at the current HEAD. Committing the guard moves HEAD one commit past the commit the README was generated at, so live divergence is 28 while the README records 27 and the assertion fails permanently - no regeneration can fix it, because regenerating the README and committing it repeats the same off-by-one.
new_findings.evidence: docs/state/test/state-artifacts.test.mjs:186 `assert.equal(Number(git('rev-list', '--count', 'origin/main..HEAD')), Number(ahead), ...)`; `node --test docs/state/test/state-artifacts.test.mjs` -> actual 28, expected 27; `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` = 28 vs `git rev-list --count origin/main..8e3f219` = 27 (the README's own value)
new_findings.impact: An enrolled gate is red at HEAD: `npm test` exits 1 with 902/904, so `make test` fails, which is the exact condition acceptance criterion P1 was written to prevent ('the enrolled gate cannot pass while the root gate fails'). The fix is to compare against the recorded commit: `assert.equal(Number(git('rev-list','--count',`origin/main..${sha}`)), Number(ahead), ...)`.

new_findings.finding: The gitleaks allowlist entries are prefixes of the values the scanner actually reports, not the 'exact value' the header now claims. A naked scan (empty config) reports the secrets as 64a4809e8e8a52cab6a9ff9ec53ac9bf449fd9521a55ad7ec6fd11527cd5bbf1 and GAYA_CANARY_NARRATOR_SECRET_98412_REIDRAKOVIA, while the allowlist carries the 40-character truncation and GAYA_CANARY_NARRATOR_SECRET_98412_REIDRA. The entries work because gitleaks matches allowlist regexes against the secret unanchored, which is also why the header's 'exact value' wording is not literally true.
new_findings.evidence: `gitleaks git . --config /tmp/empty-gitleaks.toml --report-format json` -> 9 findings / 6 unique secrets, printed above; .gitleaks.toml regexes list
new_findings.impact: Cosmetic on today's corpus (nothing else in the file is pattern-shaped and the two entries still suppress only their own secrets), but the comment again describes a guarantee the mechanism does not provide. Replacing the two truncated values with the full reported secrets would make the statement true and the intent legible.

gitleaks was run three times: the workspace history scan, and two synthetic control repositories under /tmp (one with the KAD config, one with an empty config) to establish what the scanner reports before and after the allowlist.
The receipt's mirror-drift line and the three gate results in claims_unverified were not re-run.
summary: Four of the five fixes are solid: the execution receipt is genuinely refreshed and its remaining known-red lines are true, the scope amendment names every path I flagged with a reason, P7 is recorded as an explicit PARTIAL with a named operator decision, and the gitleaks allowlist now matches by secret value - I reproduced that with a control in which a synthetic github-pat on the same line as an allowlisted hash is still reported. The README fix is only partial and it takes the enrolled gate down with it: the new guard compares the README's divergence against the live checkout while permitting a one-commit lag, so it fails on its own commit (28 vs 27), the CSA was left two commits behind at the same time, and npm test now exits 1 at 902/904 while the refreshed receipt still claims 904/904 and 13/13. Fix those three lines and refresh the CSA in the same commit, then the follow-up is clean.
